shortDefinition: A setting that controls how creative or random an AI model's responses are.
fullDefinition: Temperature is a parameter (typically 0 to 2) that controls the randomness of an LLM's output. At low temperature (0-0.3), the model picks the highest-probability token at each step — producing consistent, predictable output. At high temperature (0.7-1.5), it samples more randomly from possibilities — producing more creative but potentially less accurate output. Temperature is why the 'same prompt' can produce different answers.
examples: Temperature 0: best for code, facts, structured extraction
Temperature 0.7: best for creative writing, brainstorming
